title: Patch: the Worker's own answers carry the site's security headers
thread:
**Issue #4297 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #4297: Patch: the Worker's own answers carry the site's security headers
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
Some answers the site's Worker builds itself go out without the safety headers every file Cloudflare serves gets. The game's engine file is served by the Worker instead of as a plain file, and the "page not found" answers from both the game site's Worker and the dev dashboard's Worker carry no safety headers either. The dashboard's own header file is also missing the rule that forces secure connections. After this change, those answers carry the same protections, so a browser treats them with the same suspicion it treats the rest of the site.

## Why
The file Cloudflare serves for the whole game site (`apps/web/public/_headers`) sets a strict set of headers: a content policy, no framing, no content-type guessing, a strict referrer policy, and forced HTTPS. But three kinds of answers never pass through that file because the Worker makes them: the compressed engine module (`precompressedModule` sets only content type, encoding, and caching), the plain-text 404 for unknown paths, and the dashboard Worker's JSON 404. A search over the server and edge code finds no `nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options`, `Strict-Transport-Security`, or `Content-Security-Policy` set anywhere there. The dashboard's header file (`apps/admin/public/_headers`) has the same content policy family as the game's but omits `Strict-Transport-Security` entirely, while the game's file sets a year-long one. The engine module is the sharpest case: it is executable code the browser compiles, served without `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.

## Proposal
Add the site's static security headers to the three Worker-synthesized responses: the engine module answer, the site Worker's 404, and the dashboard Worker's JSON 404; and add the missing `Strict-Transport-Security` line to the dashboard's `_headers` file. Keep the existing pattern where the Worker's cache rule mirrors the `_headers` rule (already held by a test), extended to the security headers so the two cannot drift. Deliberately out of scope: proxied `/api/*` answers, which the server owns and where a ruling forbids extra headers on at least one error (R145's `invalid_code` stays byte for byte and header for header).

## Where it lands
- `apps/edge/src/routing.ts` (`precompressedModule`, and a shared header helper beside it)
- `apps/edge/src/index.ts` (the 404 branch)
- `apps/admin/worker/index.ts` (`notFound()`)
- `apps/admin/public/_headers` (the missing `Strict-Transport-Security` line)
- Tests beside the existing `#3183`/`#4011` blocks in `apps/edge/src/config.test.ts` (and the dashboard's `headers.test.ts` style), holding the Worker's headers to the `_headers` files
- SPEC: no section governs response headers today; the `_headers` files plus `static-pages.ts`/`headers.ts` (which fill the content-policy placeholders) are the contract. No ruling needed (no Hearthstone-semantics decision, no player-visible rules change).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The engine module answer carries `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and the site's framing/referrer/transport headers, verified by a test that reads them off a `precompressedModule` answer
- [ ] Both Workers' 404 answers carry the same static headers, verified by unit tests
- [ ] The dashboard's `_headers` sets `Strict-Transport-Security`, verified by the dashboard's header test
- [ ] A test holds the Worker's header set to the `_headers` files so they cannot drift (mirroring the existing cache-rule test)
- [ ] No header is added to proxied `/api/*` answers (R145's byte-for-byte error untouched)
- [ ] `pnpm --dir apps/web test` (edge project) and the admin typecheck/test pass

## Size and risks
Small: a few dozen lines plus tests, no migration, no spec change. Risk is low but real: a content policy applied to a non-HTML answer is harmless, yet headers on the wasm answer must not break `instantiateStreaming` (which needs the `application/wasm` type kept exact); the tests assert the type and encoding stay byte-identical. Rejected alternative: setting these headers in Terraform or on the container instead — the answers are synthesized at the edge, so the edge is where they must be set.

---
Suggested by @jgoetzmann-bot while the queue was empty. Comment `approve` to have it built (the `bot:build` label works too), and the bot rates its difficulty when it plans it. Comment `reject` to close it without building it.

Area: `server` (`suggestions.areas`).

Class: `security` → `priority:medium`; relabel to change it.

## Plan

_Written by `muse` (muse, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/44749929348)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

Give the three Worker-synthesized answers the game site's four placeholder-free static security headers (`X-Content-Type-Options`, `X-Frame-Options`, `Referrer-Policy`, `Strict-Transport-Security`): the engine module answer from `precompressedModule`, the site Worker's plain-text 404, and the dashboard Worker's JSON 404. Add the missing year-long `Strict-Transport-Security` line to `apps/admin/public/_headers`. Pin the Workers' header set to `apps/web/public/_headers` with tests so neither can drift, and leave every proxied `/api/*` answer byte-for-byte untouched (R145).

## Files to touch

| Path | New / change | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `apps/edge/src/routing.ts` | change | Add `SECURITY_HEADERS` (frozen 4-entry record) and `withSecurityHeaders(headers: Headers): void` beside `precompressedModule`; call it in `precompressedModule`. |
| `apps/edge/src/index.ts` | change | The `404` branch builds its `Response` through `withSecurityHeaders`. |
| `apps/admin/worker/index.ts` | change | `notFound()` sends the same four headers via its own `SECURITY_HEADERS` record (values identical to the site Worker's). |
| `apps/admin/public/_headers` | change | Add `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains` to the `/*` block. |
| `apps/edge/src/routing.test.ts` | change | `#4297` tests: module answer carries the four headers; type/encoding/cache/ETag/body unchanged. |
| `apps/edge/src/config.test.ts` | change | `#4297` drift test beside the `#3183`/`#4011` blocks: `SECURITY_HEADERS` keys and values equal the `/*` block of `apps/web/public/_headers`. |
| `apps/edge/src/index.test.ts` | change | `the Worker's routes`: 404 carries the four headers; proxied answers gain none. |
| `apps/admin/worker/index.test.ts` | change | 404 carries the four headers, pinned to `apps/web/public/_headers`; forwarded answers gain none. |
| `apps/admin/headers.test.ts` | change | Assert the new `Strict-Transport-Security` line and its equality with the game file's value. |

Do not touch: `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`, `crates/*`, `wrangler.jsonc`, `infra/`, `e2e/`, anything under `apps/web/src`, or any spec note. No spec section governs response headers today; the `_headers` files plus `apps/web/static-pages.ts` / `apps/admin/headers.ts` (which fill the CSP placeholders) are the contract. No ruling note is needed: there is no Hearthstone-semantics decision and no player-visible rules change. R145 (`spec/rulings/R0145.md`, the identical redemption error) constrains the work only negatively: the server's `/api/*` answers, including the `invalid_code` error, pass through the Workers untouched.

## Steps

1. `apps/edge/src/routing.ts`, directly below `MODULE_CACHE_CONTROL`: add the exported frozen record `SECURITY_HEADERS` with exactly these four entries, each value copied character-for-character from the `/*` block of `apps/web/public/_headers`: `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`, `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains`. Add `export function withSecurityHeaders(headers: Headers): void`, which sets each entry on the passed `Headers` (copy the comment style of `MODULE_CACHE_CONTROL`: `#4297`, why the Worker sets them, and that CSP is excluded because its `connect-src` is a per-build `%CONNECT_SRC%` placeholder filled by `static-pages.ts`, which the edge cannot reproduce). Do not include `Content-Security-Policy` or `Permissions-Policy`: the acceptance set is exactly these four.
2. Same file, `precompressedModule`: after the `Cache-Control` lines and before the `return`, call `withSecurityHeaders(headers)`. Leave the non-200 early return (`return stored`) exactly as it is, so a 304/404 from `ASSETS` keeps its identity.
3. `apps/edge/src/index.ts`: import `withSecurityHeaders` from `./routing.ts` (extend the existing import list) and change the 404 branch to build the answer through it: create `const headers = new Headers(); withSecurityHeaders(headers); return new Response("Not found", { status: 404, headers });`. Body text and status stay identical. Do not touch the `isModulePath`, `isServerPath`, or `server(env).fetch` paths.
4. `apps/admin/worker/index.ts`: add an exported `SECURITY_HEADERS` record with the same four names and values as routing.ts (comment: `#4297`, kept equal to the site Worker's set; the test pins both to `apps/web/public/_headers`), and pass a copy as `headers` in `notFound()`'s `Response.json` init. Error code, message, and status stay identical. Do not touch `forwards` or the `SITE.fetch` pass-through.
5. `apps/admin/public/_headers`, `/*` block: append `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains` after the `Permissions-Policy` line, copying the game file's value exactly.
6. `apps/edge/src/routing.test.ts`, in the `#3183` describe (copy the existing `precompressedModule` test pattern): add `it("#4297 sets the static security headers on the served module", ...)` asserting the four headers on a 200 answer, and assert `Content-Type` is still `application/wasm`, `Content-Encoding` still `br`, and the body bytes unchanged. Keep the existing `toBe(stored)` pass-through test unmodified.
7. `apps/edge/src/config.test.ts`, after the `#3183 the module's cache rule` describe: add `describe("#4297 the Worker's security headers", ...)` with one `it` asserting `Object.keys(SECURITY_HEADERS).sort()` is exactly the four names, and one `it` parsing `apps/web/public/_headers`' `/*` block (same regex style as the cache-rule test, or the block parser in `apps/web/src/net/cloudflare-config.test.ts`) and asserting each entry equals the file's value for that name.
8. `apps/edge/src/index.test.ts`, `the Worker's routes`: extend the 404 test to assert the four header values on the answer, and extend the forwards test with `expect(answer.headers.get("X-Content-Type-Options")).toBeNull()` and the same for `Strict-Transport-Security`, proving proxied answers gain nothing.
9. `apps/admin/worker/index.test.ts`: in the 404 block, assert the four headers on `notFound()` answers; read `apps/web/public/_headers` (path: `join(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "../../web/public/_headers")`, parsed with the `header()` line-scan style of `apps/admin/headers.test.ts`) and assert each of the four equals the file's value, so the admin copy cannot drift from the site Worker's source of truth. In the forwards-hands-on test, assert the returned answer carries no `X-Content-Type-Options` header (pass-through untouched).
10. `apps/admin/headers.test.ts`: add `it("#4297 forces HTTPS for a year, like the game site", ...)` asserting `header(filled, "Strict-Transport-Security")` is `max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains`, and assert it equals the game file's value read from `apps/web/public/_headers`.

## Tests

- `apps/edge/src/routing.test.ts`, `#4297` module-header tests: four headers present with exact values; `Content-Type`/`Content-Encoding`/body byte-identical; 304/404 identity pass-through still `toBe(stored)`.
- `apps/edge/src/config.test.ts`, `#4297` drift test: key set exact; every value equals the game `_headers` `/*` block.
- `apps/edge/src/index.test.ts`, extended routes tests: site 404 carries the four headers; proxied `/api/*` answer gains none.
- `apps/admin/worker/index.test.ts`, extended 404 tests: JSON 404 carries the four headers with values pinned to the game `_headers` file; error shape (`not_found` code, message, 404) unchanged; forwarded answers gain none.
- `apps/admin/headers.test.ts`, `#4297` HSTS test: line present, value exact, equal to the game file's.
- Commands (from the repo root unless noted): `pnpm exec vitest run --project edge`; `pnpm --dir apps/admin test worker/index.test.ts headers.test.ts`; then `pnpm --dir apps/admin test build.test.ts` (two real Vite builds, slow, proves the edited `_headers` still fills cleanly); `pnpm --dir apps/edge typecheck`; `pnpm --dir apps/admin typecheck`; `pnpm exec eslint apps/edge apps/admin`. No `cargo jackioh spec check` (no ruling added or cited).

## Done when

- [ ] `precompressedModule` answers carry the four headers with `application/wasm` + `br` intact.
- [ ] Both Workers' 404s carry the same four headers; error bodies/statuses unchanged.
- [ ] Dashboard `_headers` sets the year-long HSTS; its test pins the value to the game file's.
- [ ] A test pins the Workers' header set to the `_headers` file(s) so values cannot drift.
- [ ] Proxied `/api/*` answers (including R145's error) gain no header: covered by the pass-through assertions.
- [ ] Edge suite, the three admin test files, both typechecks, and eslint are green.

## Risks

- `instantiateStreaming` needs `Content-Type: application/wasm` exactly: the change only adds headers, never alters type/encoding/body, and the tests assert all three stay byte-identical.
- CSP is deliberately not set on Worker answers: its `connect-src` is a per-build placeholder the edge cannot fill, and a hardcoded CSP would break hosts or drift; a CSP on a non-HTML answer buys nothing.
- `Permissions-Policy` is deliberately not set: the issue's acceptance set is exactly the four headers (nosniff + framing/referrer/transport), and the drift test asserts the exact key set.
- The admin Worker duplicates the four literals (it cannot import the edge package: separate deploy units); both copies are pinned to the same `_headers` file by tests, so a drift fails loudly in both suites.
- Non-200 answers from `ASSETS` through `precompressedModule` keep identity pass-through; only the site Worker's own synthesized 404 gains headers.

## Open questions

None. Every choice above follows the issue text; the two exclusions (CSP, `Permissions-Policy`) are recorded under Risks with reasons.

Add `export function withSecurityHeaders(headers: Headers): void`, which sets each entry on the passed `Headers` (copy the comment style of `MODULE_CACHE_CONTROL`: `#4297`, why the Worker sets them, and that CSP is excluded because its `connect-src` is a per-build `%CONNECT_SRC%` placeholder filled by `static-pages.ts`, which the edge cannot reproduce). 3. `apps/edge/src/index.ts`: import `withSecurityHeaders` from `./routing.ts` (extend the existing import list) and change the 404 branch to build the answer through it: create `const headers = new Headers(); withSecurityHeaders(headers); return new Response("Not found", { status: 404, headers });`. Body text and status stay identical. Do not touch the `isModulePath`, `isServerPath`, or `server(env).fetch` paths.
4. `apps/admin/worker/index.ts`: add an exported `SECURITY_HEADERS` record with the same four names and values as routing.ts (comment: `#4297`, kept equal to the site Worker's set; the test pins both to `apps/web/public/_headers`), and pass a copy as `headers` in `notFound()`'s `Response.json` init. Error code, message, and status stay identical. Do not touch `forwards` or the `SITE.fetch` pass-through.
5. `apps/admin/public/_headers`, `/*` block: append `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains` after the `Permissions-Policy` line, copying the game file's value exactly.
6. `apps/edge/src/routing.test.ts`, in the `#3183` describe (copy the existing `precompressedModule` test pattern): add `it("#4297 sets the static security headers on the served module", ...)` asserting the four headers on a 200 answer, and assert `Content-Type` is still `application/wasm`, `Content-Encoding` still `br`, and the body bytes unchanged. Keep the existing `toBe(stored)` pass-through test unmodified.
7. `apps/edge/src/config.test.ts`, after the `#3183 the module's cache rule` describe: add `describe("#4297 the Worker's security headers", ...)` with one `it` asserting `Object.keys(SECURITY_HEADERS).sort()` is exactly the four names, and one `it` parsing `apps/web/public/_headers`' `/*` block (same regex style as the cache-rule test, or the block parser in `apps/web/src/net/cloudflare-config.test.ts`) and asserting each entry equals the file's value for that name.

- `apps/edge/src/routing.test.ts`, `#4297` module-header tests: four headers present with exact values; `Content-Type`/`Content-Encoding`/body byte-identical; 304/404 identity pass-through still `toBe(stored)`.
- `apps/edge/src/config.test.ts`, `#4297` drift test: key set exact; every value equals the game `_headers` `/*` block.
- `apps/edge/src/index.test.ts`, extended routes tests: site 404 carries the four headers; proxied `/api/*` answer gains none.
- `apps/admin/worker/index.test.ts`, extended 404 tests: JSON 404 carries the four headers with values pinned to the game `_headers` file; error shape (`not_found` code, message, 404) unchanged; forwarded answers gain none.
- `apps/admin/headers.test.ts`, `#4297` HSTS test: line present, value exact, equal to the game file's.

No `cargo jackioh spec check` (no ruling added or cited).

## Done when

- [ ] `precompressedModule` answers carry the four headers with `application/wasm` + `br` intact.
- [ ] Both Workers' 404s carry the same four headers; error bodies/statuses unchanged.
- [ ] Dashboard `_headers` sets the year-long HSTS; its test pins the value to the game file's.
- [ ] A test pins the Workers' header set to the `_headers` file(s) so values cannot drift.
- [ ] Proxied `/api/*` answers (including R145's error) gain no header: covered by the pass-through assertions.
- [ ] Edge suite, the three admin test files, both typechecks, and eslint are green.

## Risks

- `instantiateStreaming` needs `Content-Type: application/wasm` exactly: the change only adds headers, never alters type/encoding/body, and the tests assert all three stay byte-identical.
- CSP is deliberately not set on Worker answers: its `connect-src` is a per-build placeholder the edge cannot fill, and a hardcoded CSP would break hosts or drift; a CSP on a non-HTML answer buys nothing.
- `Permissions-Policy` is deliberately not set: the issue's acceptance set is exactly the four headers (nosniff + framing/referrer/transport), and the drift test asserts the exact key set.
- The admin Worker duplicates the four literals (it cannot import the edge package: separate deploy units); both copies are pinned to the same `_headers` file by tests, so a drift fails loudly in both suites.
- Non-200 answers from `ASSETS` through `precompressedModule` keep identity pass-through; only the site Worker's own synthesized 404 gains headers.

## Open questions

None. Every choice above follows the issue text; the two exclusions (CSP, `Permissions-Policy`) are recorded under Risks with reasons.
